cohort: 300 pregnant women admitted for delivery at a hospital in Telangana, India, divided into two groups: 150 teenagers (13-19 years old) and 150 adults (20-29 years old).
finding: Teenage mothers had lower socioeconomic status, less education, fewer antenatal checkups, and were more likely to experience adverse outcomes like anemia, eclampsia, fetal distress, prolonged labor, cesarean section, and instrumental delivery compared to adult mothers.
